set.notes: [residency_at_reason: director-unidentified] [V16-B2 reclassify direct_training -> residency_at; endpoints flipped to person->institution per residency_at semantics] Leffall completed a senior fellowship in surgical oncology at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (1957-1959), the first African American to hold such a fellowship there. He was directed toward MSK by his Howard mentor Jack White (referral, not preceptor). No individual MSK fellowship PD/APD with a documented structural title is identifiable in the public record for this fellowship slot, so this is a residency_at fallback rather than direct_training. The fellowship bridges the independent Howard training trunk into the established oncology cluster (MSK already connected to the James Ewing Society and Memorial Hospital for Cancer and Allied Diseases). Evidence: PMID 18481473 (J Natl Med Assoc 2008), content-matched for the fellowship. Excluded from the person-person lineage projection by construction (residency_at + institution endpoint).

set.notes: [residency_at_reason: mentorless-by-committee] [V16-B2 reclassify direct_training -> residency_at; endpoints flipped to person->institution; temporal_range normalized '1912-c. 1917' -> '1912-1917'] Frederick Amasa Coller (1887-1964) graduated from Harvard Medical School (1912) and was appointed the first surgical resident at Massachusetts General Hospital, chosen by unanimous vote of all attending surgeons (i.e. mentorless-by-committee: no single named PD/APD directed the appointment). He served in WWI in France with the Harvard Medical Unit under Harvey Cushing, then joined the University of Michigan in 1920. Evidence: PMID 14036574 (Adie, Ann Surg 1961;154(Suppl):18-24), content-matched: Coller first appointed intern on the West Surgical Service at MGH July 1912, then surgical residency. Excluded from the person-person lineage projection by construction (residency_at + institution endpoint).
